title: Pasta alla Zozzona
subtitle: Rome's combined pasta: guanciale, sausage, tomatoes, and egg yolks
excerpt: Pasta alla zozzona is an unofficial Roman pasta that combines the elements of the city's four canonical sauces: guanciale from amatriciana, egg yolks from carbonara, sausage from gricia, and tomatoes. The name means roughly 'filthy' or 'indulgent'. It is richer and more substantial than any one of the sauces it draws from.
sourceNotes: Pasta alla zozzona is a contemporary Roman trattoria dish that combines elements from Rome's four canonical pasta sauces. The name (from zozza: dirty, indulgent) reflects its rule-breaking combination. It has become popular in Roman trattorias from the 2000s onward, particularly in the Testaccio and Trastevere neighbourhoods.

content.text: Pasta alla zozzona is a Roman pasta that breaks the rules. It combines guanciale, sausage, tomatoes, and egg yolks: drawing from carbonara, amatriciana, and gricia at once. The egg yolks go in off the heat, just as in carbonara. The pan must be off the heat before the eggs are added. Toss fast to avoid scrambling.
Cook the pork and make the sauce
Start the guanciale in a cold wide pan over medium heat. Render for 6 to 8 minutes until golden and crisp. Add the sausage meat and cook, breaking it up, for 5 minutes until browned.

If using white wine, add it and let it evaporate for 1 to 2 minutes. Add the tomatoes, crush with a spoon, and simmer for 12 to 15 minutes until the sauce has thickened. Season lightly: the guanciale and sausage add their own salt.
Prepare the egg mixture and finish
In a bowl, whisk together the 4 egg yolks, Parmigiano Reggiano, and black pepper until smooth.
Cook the rigatoni in well-salted boiling water until 1 minute short of al dente. Reserve a generous cup of pasta water, then drain.

Add the rigatoni to the pan with the tomato-pork sauce. Toss over high heat for 1 minute. Take the pan completely off the heat. Add the egg yolk mixture, tossing vigorously while adding pasta water a little at a time. The eggs should form a creamy coating, not scrambled curds. If the pan looks dry, add more pasta water and keep tossing. Serve immediately.

items.symptom: Eggs scramble when added to the sauce
items.cause: The pan was still on the heat when the eggs went in, or the sauce was too hot
items.fix: The pan must be completely off the heat. Let it cool for 30 seconds after removing from the hob before adding eggs. Toss fast with pasta water to control the temperature.

items.symptom: Sauce is too acidic from the tomatoes
items.fix: Simmer the tomato base for at least 15 minutes before adding pasta. The acid from the tomatoes needs time to mellow.

items.symptom: Dish is too heavy and rich
items.cause: Too much guanciale and sausage relative to tomato and pasta
items.fix: In zozzona the richness is deliberate: but balance by not adding extra cheese at the table.

content.text: Zozzona became a recognised dish in Roman trattorias in the 2000s. It is most linked with the Testaccio area, where the old working-class food tradition is still strong. The name means dirty or messy in Roman dialect. This fits: the dish is rich, heavily sauced, and breaks the rules that govern carbonara and amatriciana. It is the cook's pasta, not the purist's.
